etymologies.etymologyHTML: From French procédure, from Old French, from Latin procedere (“to go forward, proceed”); see proceed.

definitions.definition: A particular method for performing a task.

quote.citation: 2014 June 14, “It's a gas”, in The Economist, volume 411, number 8891:
quote.text: One of the hidden glories of Victorian engineering is proper drains. Isolating a city’s effluent and shipping it away in underground sewers has probably saved more lives than any medical procedure except vaccination.

definitions.definition: A series of small tasks or steps taken to accomplish an end.
(uncountable) The set of established forms or methods of an organized body for accomplishing a certain task or tasks.
The steps taken in an action or other legal proceeding.

quote.citation: 1832, [Isaac Taylor], Saturday Evening. […], London: Holdsworth and Ball, →OCLC:

1627 (indicated as 1626), Francis [Bacon], “(please specify the page, or |century=I to X)”, in Sylua Syluarum: Or A Naturall Historie. In Ten Centuries. […], London:  […]  William Rawley […]; [p]rinted by J[ohn] H[aviland] for William Lee […], →OCLC:
quote.text: There is not any known Substance, but Earth, and the Procedure of Earth (as Tile, Stone, &c.) that yeeldeth any Moss or Herby Substance.

definitions.definition: (computing) A subroutine or function coded to perform a specific task, but does not return a value.
